clue.text: Beef embargo on opening English plant

indicators.note: an opening is where a word begins, so only the first letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: a cow is a beef animal
an embargo is a ban on trade
first letter of English

explanation.surface: A ban on British beef, imposed at the start of the export trouble, reads like a farming news story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the pieces one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowbane is a poisonous waterside plant, also called water hemlock, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Rye fieldsman?

blocks.note: surface reading: a fielder playing cricket at Rye, the Sussex town
setter's reading: the one in Salinger's novel about the field of rye, as in its title

explanation.walkthrough: Rye is a Sussex town, so a fieldsman there sounds like a cricketer. The novel 'The Catcher in the Rye' supplies the other sense, and a catcher is also a fielder in baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcher is a fielding player who catches the ball, and Salinger's title puts one in the rye.

clue.text: Cause of fading light in Ireland?

definitions.text: Cause of fading light in Ireland?

blocks.note: surface reading: why a candle or lamp grows dim
setter's reading: an Irish county whose name splits into a burnt-down wick

explanation.walkthrough: A candle wick burnt down low makes the flame fade; the two words run together name a county south of Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicklow is a county on the east coast of Ireland, and its name reads as a low wick.

clue.text: Stone entrance

blocks.note: first meaning: a banded semi-precious gemstone
second meaning: read as two words, an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A stone entrance, like a carved portal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense needs the answer split as A GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a variety of chalcedony used as a gem, and a gate is a way in.

clue.text: Unusually able to speak in great detail

indicators.note: unusually means not in the usual way, so the letters are not in their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Someone unusually able to talk at great length and in detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate describes something worked out with many careful, intricate parts.

clue.text: Aircraft may be carrying one map

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so the outer word wraps the rest

blocks.note: 'may be' boils down to the verb be
Roman numeral for one
a plan is a map or drawing of a place

explanation.surface: A plane may be carrying a single map for its navigator.
explanation.definitionFit: A biplane is a type of aircraft with two pairs of wings stacked one above the other.

clue.text: Count on the piano

definitions.note: describes the man by his instrument

blocks.note: first meaning: the jazz bandleader known by the noble title Count
second meaning: the same man was a pianist, leading from the keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone counting the beats while sitting at the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb about keeping time, but it is the nickname of the American jazz pianist William Basie.
explanation.definitionFit: William 'Count' Basie led his big band from the piano stool, so both phrases fit him.

clue.text: Spread 3 on shore

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed beneath, so the first-named piece is written after the one named second

blocks.note: to shore up is to prop, and a shore is a prop
the answer to 3 down

explanation.surface: Stone spread along the seashore.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece below the second; 'shore' is a support, not the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate is to spread or disseminate, as with ideas or plants.

clue.text: Shrink from the mention of a record collector

indicators.note: a mention is something spoken, so it is the sound of the words that counts

blocks.note: an annalist compiles annals, historical records

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at any mention of a vinyl record collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like a verb (recoil) but is slang for a psychiatrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink is slang for a psychiatrist, and an analyst is a psychoanalyst.

clue.text: She's among the lean or spare type

indicators.note: among means sitting in the middle of the following words

blocks.note: runs from the last letter of the first word through the next two
surface padding: spare means thin, echoing lean

explanation.surface: She belongs among the thin or skinny types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare type' is surface padding describing the lean; spare here means thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a woman's name, so she is a fair stand-in.

clue.text: Music performance by Felix in knitted coat

definitions.note: a toccata is a keyboard piece, here loosely a piece performed

indicators.note: knitted wool is worked into new loops, so the letters are worked into a new order
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
Felix the Cat is a famous cartoon cat

explanation.surface: A cat named Felix performs a musical turn while dressed in a knitted coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Felix is the cat of the old cartoons, so any 'Felix' in a crossword may be a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a showy keyboard composition designed to display a performer's touch and speed.

clue.text: Keeping one in parental affection

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: storge is the Greek word for the natural love of parents for children
a means one

explanation.surface: Holding a child in parental love sounds like a tender family scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek word for family love is a rare borrowing into English that crossword setters occasionally use.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is the act of keeping things put away, so the nouns match.

clue.text: "Flower of Perdition" -  point made by an archbishop

blocks.note: perdition is damnation, eternal punishment in hell
Ebor is the signature of the Archbishop of York
E for east, a compass point

explanation.surface: A grim religious tract titled 'Flower of Perdition' gets its point from an archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archbishop of York signs himself Ebor, from the Latin name for York; 'made by' sets the compass point beside him.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellebore is a winter-flowering plant such as the Christmas rose, so it is a kind of flower.

clue.text: Race of mercenary Anglo-Saxons

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the letters are taken from within the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A historical note about a people descended from hired Saxon warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: Aryan was an old term for a supposed ancestral people or ethnic group, now discredited.

clue.text: Atkinson on war training

indicators.note: training puts things through drills, so the letters are drilled into a new formation

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A comedian named Atkinson goes into military training for a war.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowan Atkinson is the British comic actor who plays Mr Bean.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian's first name stands in for his surname, as solvers fill in the familiar pairing.

clue.text: Mobile phones, yet recently introduced

definitions.note: a phrase for those recently introduced, standing for the plural noun

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters move about

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Mobile phones were, at the time, a newly introduced gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' looks like part of 'mobile phones', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophytes are newcomers or novices, people recently brought into a church or activity.

clue.text: A party bloomer -  providing mineral!

blocks.note: taken as written
Lab is short for the Labour Party
a bloomer is a flower, here the aster

explanation.surface: A blunder at a party ends up providing a valuable find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder or a loaf, but it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft white form of gypsum, a mineral used for carving.

clue.text: Take choir trip to Jerusalem, perhaps

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A church choir is taken on a pilgrimage to the Holy City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerusalem' is not the city but the Jerusalem artichoke, a knobbly root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jerusalem artichoke is one kind of artichoke, so 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Taking a gorgeous creature to love retreat is cheating

blocks.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a nest is a cosy retreat

explanation.surface: Whisking a beautiful lover away to a secret hideaway is infidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest describes deceitful behaviour, which is what cheating is.

clue.text: Drawing weight needs raising help first

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising lifts the word so it reads upward, backwards

blocks.note: aid is help
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Pulling a heavy weight needs help to lift it first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the help piece before the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simple explanatory drawing or sketch.

clue.text: Grant given to Kent for approaching the Channel?

blocks.note: Kent is in the south-east of England
an award is a grant of money

explanation.surface: A grant is given to the county of Kent for work on the Channel approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is the English county facing France across the English Channel; it stands for SE, its corner of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaward means towards the sea, which for Kent is towards the Channel; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Disabled without one, turn to a modern mode of communication

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other
turn means the combined letters are read the other way

blocks.note: lame means disabled in the legs
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone unable to get about, without company, turns to a new way of keeping in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without one' reads as lacking one, but it means outside one. The I goes in after L, giving LIAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Email was, when this was set, a newly popular way of sending messages over computers.

clue.text: Half light in the river where there's a bridge

indicators.note: half means only one of the two halves of the word is kept
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the Avon is the classic crossword river
light as a verb is ignite, and its first half is kept

explanation.surface: Half the light falls in the river by a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept letters go in after AV. The famous bridge is the Pont d'Avignon of the French song.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon in southern France is famous for its medieval bridge, Pont Saint-Bénezet, celebrated in a children's song.

clue.text: A soldier in a pub - it stands to reason

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier drinking in the pub is just what you'd expect.
explanation.walkthrough: The local is British slang for the nearby pub one regularly drinks in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stands to reason follows by sound argument, which is what logical means.

clue.text: Like the bilge in a Shaw play?

indicators.note: play means loose movement, so these letters are free to move around

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Is the bilge a character in a George Bernard Shaw drama?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bilge' suggests nonsense, as in a bad play, but it is the bottom of a ship, often swilling with water.
explanation.definitionFit: The bilge of a ship collects seawater, so it is typically flooded and swilling.

clue.text: Selection starts with freezing out of Livingstone, making you want to throw up

definitions.text: making you want to throw up

indicators.note: starts means only the first letter of the word is used
out of here means placed around the outside of the next piece

blocks.note: first letter of Selection
icing is freezing over
Ken Livingstone, then Mayor of London

explanation.surface: A politician being frozen out of a selection contest is enough to make his supporters ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone was a left-wing London politician whom the Labour Party tried to keep off its mayoral shortlist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickening describes something that causes nausea, the feeling of being about to vomit.

clue.text: Stop about right? On the contrary

definitions.note: with 'right' just before it: the opposite of being right, so going astray

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer word goes around

blocks.note: to stay is to stop or halt
R for right

explanation.surface: Someone says stop is about right, and is contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' does double duty: it gives R and, with 'On the contrary', defines wandering from the right path.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander off the correct course, the reverse of keeping right.

clue.text: Bore heard with enthusiasm

indicators.note: heard means we go by the sound of the words, not their spelling

blocks.note: eager means keen, full of enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A tedious person is listened to with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is not a dull person but a tidal wave running up a river, such as on the Severn or Trent.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a dialect name for a tidal bore, a wave surging upstream.

clue.text: He sells last lot included for development

indicators.note: developing something changes its form, so the letters are reshaped
included means one word is put inside another

blocks.note: the rear is the last part
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: An estate agent sells the final plot of land included in a building scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: A realtor is the American term for an estate agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A realtor sells property for clients, so the phrase works as a description of the job.

clue.text: Love racing for a change -  that's life!

definitions.note: organic means relating to living things

indicators.note: a change of order means the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone who loves horse racing, trying something different, shrugs that it's just how things go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's life!' reads as a resigned shrug, but it defines what is living.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic matter comes from living organisms, so organic describes what has life.

clue.text: Humble dwelling following fashion - no ostentation

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first-named piece is written second

blocks.note: a mode is a fashion or style
a pigsty is the humblest of homes

explanation.surface: A modest home that ignores fashion shows no showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is the quality of not showing off, the absence of ostentation.

clue.text: Enter failure against article by student out of time

indicators.note: a failure is a breakdown, so these letters break down and are rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
the indefinite article
L for learner, the plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A student who fails to enter an exam in time is up against it.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for a learner, from the L plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal things exist outside time, without beginning or end.
